correctness.rationale: The integer edge-multiplicity matrix is realizable if and only if its imbalance is zero or a single endpoint difference and its positive-degree support is weakly connected. Balanced matrices decompose into two directed 3-cycles and three opposite-edge pairs, giving B(z). Each of the six imbalance sectors bijects with balanced matrices with one chosen edge positive, giving A(z). All disconnected possibilities are exhausted by multi-vertex loops, a reciprocally joined pair with an isolated loop, or an imbalanced joined pair with an isolated loop. The subtraction and leading coefficient were algebraically checked. Replaying verify.py checks direct word enumeration n<=9, independent Euler-matrix enumeration n<=13, and the exact reduced rational identity. Finite tests are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2010 balanced Markov type result and 2015 asymptotic profile theorem cover cyclic/balanced exact counts and leading-order linear behavior, but not the exact six imbalanced sectors with weak-connectivity corrections needed for an all-length ternary linear OGF. The closest published exact binary profile result explicitly excludes nonbinary alphabets. The full 2012 expanded paper remains inaccessible and is a specific residual risk.
residual_risks: The expanded 2012 IEEE paper was inspected only at abstract level; an exact linear enumeration implicit in its full text could cover the claim.
An earlier unindexed exact ternary Markov-type/quasipolynomial formula or a table under different terminology may exist.
The known cyclic leading constant and linear/cyclic asymptotic factor already imply the leading coefficient; novelty rests on the complete exact all-length rational OGF and connectivity corrections.

value.rationale: Adjacent-pair multiplicity profiles form a canonical complete-read reconstruction invariant. The first nonbinary (three-letter) full all-length enumeration yields an exact optimal profile-distinguishable code size and resolves the finer effects of free endpoints, 3-cycles, and isolated-support obstructions that asymptotic results ignore. The exact coefficients and period-six quasipolynomial structure are useful for finite-block benchmarks; the result is not merely a relabeling of the binary or cyclic formula.
